evidence.alignment: All three technologies target high-growth areas in biopharmaceuticals and healthcare AI, and declining markets are avoided; however, all technologies are scheduled to complete deployment at or after their market boom windows, meaning the roadmap misses peak market timing by 2-3.75 years on average.
evidence.sequencing: Dependency chains are structurally respected (T02 precedes T03 and T01 with no violations), but ADC and mass spectrometry are both planned to start and complete in 2030-Q1 with zero development duration, which is unrealistic given their TRL levels and complexity.
evidence.investment: The highest-urgency, highest-market-opportunity technology (T02) is correctly assigned Strategic tier, and ADC (T03) is also Strategic given strong market and fit scores; mass spectrometry at High tier is proportionally appropriate, and the budget remains unspent suggesting under-allocation or planning incompleteness.
evidence.coherence: The three technologies form a coherent narrative: AI data analytics enables downstream drug delivery optimization (ADC) and precision measurement (mass spectrometry), reflecting a logical research-to-deployment arc within the biopharma/diagnostics domain.
evidence.balance: The portfolio is heavily skewed toward a single reference endpoint (2030-Q1) for all technologies, with no short-term deliverables and zero budget utilization, resulting in concentrated temporal and financial risk with no early-stage or exploratory bets to diversify the portfolio.

strengths: Dependency structure is correctly enforced with zero violations, ensuring T02 foundational AI capability precedes dependent technologies T03 and T01.
Investment tier assignments are rationally calibrated to market opportunity and strategic fit scores, with the highest-scoring technology receiving the highest tier.
weaknesses: All technologies are scheduled to complete at 2030-Q1, well after their respective market boom windows (2026-Q2, 2027-Q3, 2028-Q1), resulting in a mean timing error of 2.75 years and likely missed first-mover advantages.

Zero budget has been allocated or spent despite a substantial total budget, and the portfolio contains only 3 technologies all converging on a single timeline point, reflecting poor portfolio breadth and financial planning.
missing_technologies: Next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms for genomic diagnostics to complement ADC targeting
Digital biomarker and wearable sensor integration to feed the AI data stream analytics pipeline
Bioinformatics / multi-omics data integration middleware bridging mass spectrometry outputs to AI analytics
investment_issues: Total budget spend is 0, indicating no investment has been committed or modeled, rendering the budget constraint meaningless and the strategy incomplete.
With only two tiers used (Strategic and High) across three technologies, there is no exploratory or low-tier investment to hedge against uncertainty or fund early-stage research.
timing_issues: T02 (AI 기반 의료 데이터 스트림 분석) has a 3.75-year lag behind its 2026-Q2 boom, meaning the roadmap enters the market well past peak opportunity.
T01 and T03 both have zero planned development duration (2030-Q1 to 2030-Q1), which is infeasible for TRL 7 technologies requiring validation and scale-up.
No technology in the portfolio has an early deployment window before 2030, leaving the organization with no near-term market presence or revenue generation.
